events.label: McMurdo says Scanlan should not take it upon himself to ask such things

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Who are you that you should take it on yourself to ask such things?”

events.label: McMurdo shows sudden and dangerous anger in his gray eyes from behind his glasses
Scanlan says no offense and that the boys will think none the worse

communicates.content: “All right, mate, no offense meant. The boys will think none the worse of you, whatever you may have done.”

events.label: Scanlan asks where McMurdo is bound for now

communicates.content: “Where are you bound for now?”

events.label: McMurdo says he is bound for Vermissa

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Vermissa.”

events.label: Scanlan says Vermissa is the third halt down the line and asks where McMurdo is staying

communicates.content: “That’s the third halt down the line. Where are you staying?”

events.label: McMurdo has Scanlan hold the address near the oil lamp
Scanlan provides an address on Sheridan Street and says it is a boarding house recommended from Chicago

communicates.content: “Here is the address—Jacob Shafter, Sheridan Street. It’s a boarding house that was recommended by a man I knew in Chicago.”

events.label: Scanlan says Vermissa is out of his beat and that he lives at Hobson’s Patch where they are drawing up

communicates.content: “Well, I don’t know it; but Vermissa is out of my beat. I live at Hobson’s Patch, and that’s here where we are drawing up.”

events.label: Scanlan advises McMurdo to go to the Union House and see Boss McGinty if he is in trouble in Vermissa

communicates.content: “But, say, there’s one bit of advice I’ll give you before we part: If you’re in trouble in Vermissa, go straight to the Union House and see Boss McGinty.”

events.label: Scanlan identifies Boss McGinty as Bodymaster of Vermissa Lodge and says nothing can happen unless Black Jack McGinty wants it

communicates.content: “He is the Bodymaster of Vermissa Lodge, and nothing can happen in these parts unless Black Jack McGinty wants it.”

events.label: Scanlan says so long and suggests they may meet in lodge

communicates.content: “So long, mate! Maybe we’ll meet in lodge one of these evenings.”

events.label: Scanlan warns McMurdo that if he is in trouble he should go to Boss McGinty

communicates.content: “But mind my words: If you are in trouble, go to Boss McGinty.”

events.label: Scanlan descends from the train and McMurdo is left alone to his thoughts
McMurdo turns and sees one of the policemen staring out at the fiery waste
A policeman says hell must be something like the scene and asks whether there are worse devils down yonder

communicates.content: “For that matter,” said the other policeman, “I allow that hell must be something like that. If there are worse devils down yonder than some we could name, it’s more than I’d expect.”

events.label: A policeman asks McMurdo whether he is new to this part

communicates.content: “I guess you are new to this part, young man?”

events.label: McMurdo responds surly and says what if he is

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Well, what if I am?”

events.label: McMurdo is advised to be careful in choosing friends and not to begin with Mike Scanlan or his gang

communicates.content: “Just this, mister, that I should advise you to be careful in choosing your friends. I don’t think I’d begin with Mike Scanlan or his gang if I were you.”

events.label: McMurdo asks what it is to the policeman who his friends are

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “What the hell is it to you who are my friends?”

events.label: McMurdo’s angry response causes every head in the carriage to turn toward the altercation
McMurdo says he did not ask for advice and that the policeman would have to wait a long time

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Did I ask you for your advice, or did you think me such a sucker that I couldn’t move without it?”

events.label: McMurdo says the policeman should speak only when spoken to

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “You speak when you are spoken to, and by the Lord you’d have to wait a long time if it was me!”

events.label: McMurdo thrusts out his face and grins at the patrolmen like a snarling dog
The policemen are taken aback by the vehemence of their friendly advances being rejected
A policeman says no offense, stranger

communicates.content: “No offense, stranger,” said one.

events.label: A policeman says the warning is for the stranger's own good because he is new to the place

communicates.content: “It was a warning for your own good, seeing that you are, by your own showing, new to the place.”

events.label: McMurdo says he is new to the place but not new to the policemen and their kind

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “I’m new to the place; but I’m not new to you and your kind!”

events.label: McMurdo says the policemen shove advice in when nobody asks for it

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “I guess you’re the same in all places, shoving your advice in when nobody asks for it.”

events.label: A policeman says they may see more of McMurdo before long

communicates.content: “Maybe we’ll see more of you before very long,” said one of the patrolmen with a grin.

events.label: McMurdo says the policeman is hand-picked if he is a judge

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “You’re a real hand-picked one, if I am a judge.”

events.label: McMurdo says he is not afraid of the policeman and that he should not think it

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “I’m not afraid of you, and don’t you think it!”

events.label: McMurdo says his name is Jack McMurdo and gives his address as Jacob Shafter’s on Sheridan Street, Vermissa

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “My name’s Jack McMurdo—see? If you want me, you’ll find me at Jacob Shafter’s on Sheridan Street, Vermissa; so I’m not hiding from you, am I?”

events.label: McMurdo says day or night he dares to look at the policemen in the face

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Day or night I dare to look the like of you in the face—don’t make any mistake about that!”

events.label: Miners show sympathy and admiration at McMurdo’s demeanour while the policemen shrug and renew conversation
The train runs into the ill-lit station, and there is a general clearing because Vermissa is the largest town on the line
McMurdo picks up his leather gripsack and is about to start off into the darkness
A miner accosts McMurdo and comments that he knows how to speak to the cops

communicates.content: “By Gar, mate! you know how to speak to the cops,” he said in a voice of awe.

events.label: The miner says it was grand to hear McMurdo and offers to carry his grip and show the road

communicates.content: “It was grand to hear you. Let me carry your grip and show you the road. I’m passing Shafter’s on the way to my own shack.”

events.label: Other miners say friendly good-nights as they pass from the platform
A guide points to a saloon and identifies it as the Union House and says Jack McGinty is the boss there

communicates.content: “That’s the Union House,” said the guide, pointing to one saloon which rose almost to the dignity of being a hotel. “Jack McGinty is the boss there.”

events.label: McMurdo asks what sort of man Jack McGinty is

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “What sort of a man is he?”

events.label: The miner says McMurdo could not have heard of him because McMurdo is a stranger in these parts

communicates.content: “Have you never heard of the boss?” “How could I have heard of him when you know that I am a stranger in these parts?”

events.label: The miner says Jack McGinty’s name is known across the country and has been in the papers

communicates.content: “Well, I thought his name was known clear across the country. It’s been in the papers often enough.”

events.label: McMurdo asks what for

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “What for?”

events.label: The miner lowers his voice and says the papers are about over the affairs

communicates.content: “Well,” the miner lowered his voice—“over the affairs.”

events.label: McMurdo asks what affairs

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “What affairs?”

events.label: The miner says the only affairs mentioned are the affairs of the Scowrers

communicates.content: “There’s only one set of affairs that you’ll hear of in these parts, and that’s the affairs of the Scowrers.”

events.label: McMurdo asks if the Scowrers are a gang of murderers

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “A gang of murderers, are they not?”

events.label: The miner cries hush and warns McMurdo he will not live long for speaking in the open street

communicates.content: “Hush, on your life!” “Man, you won’t live long in these parts if you speak in the open street like that. Many a man has had the life beaten out of him for less.”

events.label: McMurdo says he knows nothing about them and that it is only what he has read

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Well, I know nothing about them. It’s only what I have read.”

events.label: The miner says he is not saying McMurdo has not read the truth

communicates.content: “And I’m not saying that you have not read the truth.”

events.label: The miner warns McMurdo not to breathe Jack McGinty’s name in connection with killing

communicates.content: “If killing is murder, then God knows there is murder and to spare. But don’t you dare to breathe the name of Jack McGinty in connection with it, stranger; for every whisper goes back to him, and he is not one that is likely to let it pass.”

events.label: The miner directs McMurdo to the boarding house run by old Jacob Shafter

communicates.content: “Now, that’s the house you’re after, that one standing back from the street. You’ll find old Jacob Shafter that runs it as honest a man as lives in this township.”

events.label: McMurdo thanks the miner, shakes his hand, and knocks at Jacob Shafter’s door
The door is opened by a young woman
The young woman says she thought it was father

communicates.content: “I thought it was father,” said she with a pleasing little touch of a German accent.

events.label: The young woman asks whether McMurdo came to see father

communicates.content: “Did you come to see him?”

events.label: The young woman says father is down town and she expects him back every minute

communicates.content: “He is down town. I expect him back every minute.”

events.label: McMurdo says he is not in a hurry to see father and that the house was recommended to him for board

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “No, miss,” he said at last, “I’m in no hurry to see him. But your house was recommended to me for board. I thought it might suit me—and now I know it will.”

events.label: The young woman invites McMurdo inside and says she is Miss Ettie Shafter, father’s daughter, and that she runs the house

communicates.content: “Come right in, sir,” she said. “I’m Miss Ettie Shafter, Mr. Shafter’s daughter. My mother’s dead, and I run the house.”

events.label: The young woman tells McMurdo he can sit by the stove until father comes along and says father is coming

communicates.content: “You can sit down by the stove in the front room until father comes along—Ah, here he is! So you can fix things with him right away.”

events.label: An elderly heavy man comes plodding up the path
McMurdo explains his business in a few words
McMurdo says Murphy gave him the address in Chicago

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “A man of the name of Murphy had given him the address in Chicago.”

events.label: McMurdo says old Shafter’s address came from someone else

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “He in turn had had it from someone else.”

events.label: Old Shafter is ready to accept the arrangement
McMurdo agrees at once to every condition and is apparently fairly flush of money
A weekly boarding agreement is set for seven dollars a week paid in advance
McMurdo takes up residence under the roof of the Shafters as his first step toward later events
McMurdo becomes an important person at Shafter's within a week
McMurdo obtains a temporary job as a bookkeeper
Mike Scanlan visits McMurdo one evening
Mike Scanlan says McMurdo has not reported to the Bodymaster

communicates.speaker: mike_scanlan
communicates.content: I’m surprised that you’ve not reported to the Bodymaster.

events.label: Mike Scanlan asks why McMurdo has not seen Boss McGinty yet

communicates.speaker: mike_scanlan
communicates.content: Why haven’t you seen Boss McGinty yet?

events.label: McMurdo responds that he had to find a job and has been busy

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, I had to find a job. I have been busy.

events.label: Mike Scanlan tells McMurdo to find time to see Boss McGinty

communicates.speaker: mike_scanlan
communicates.content: You must find time for him if you have none for anything else. Good Lord, man!

events.label: Mike Scanlan tells McMurdo he should have registered his name at the Union House

communicates.speaker: mike_scanlan
communicates.content: you’re a fool not to have been down to the Union House and registered your name the first morning after you came here!

events.label: McMurdo says he has been a member of the lodge for over two years

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’ve been a member of the lodge for over two years, Scanlan, but I never heard that duties were so pressing as all that.

events.label: Mike Scanlan says it is the same society here and looks at McMurdo
Mike Scanlan says there was something sinister in his eyes
Mike Scanlan says McMurdo will tell him in a month’s time

communicates.speaker: mike_scanlan
communicates.content: You’ll tell me that in a month’s time.

events.label: Mike Scanlan says he hears McMurdo talked with patrolmen after the train

communicates.speaker: mike_scanlan
communicates.content: I hear you had a talk with the patrolmen after I left the train.

events.label: McMurdo says he told the hounds what he thought of them

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, yes. I told the hounds what I thought of them.

events.label: Mike Scanlan tells McMurdo to go see Boss McGinty

communicates.speaker: mike_scanlan
communicates.content: It’s not the police but you that he’ll hate if you don’t!

events.label: Mike Scanlan says McMurdo will not need to dirty his hands and leaves

communicates.speaker: mike_scanlan
communicates.content: Now, take a friend’s advice and go at once!

events.label: A boarding-house keeper beckons McMurdo into his private room
The boarding-house keeper tells McMurdo that someone slipped in before him

communicates.speaker: boarding_house_keeper
communicates.content: Vell, I vant to tell you right now that it ain’t no manner of use. There’s someone slipped in afore you.

events.label: The boarding-house keeper says Ettie told him there was someone

communicates.speaker: boarding_house_keeper
communicates.content: She told me so.

events.label: The boarding-house keeper says the man is Teddy Baldwin

communicates.speaker: boarding_house_keeper
communicates.content: It is Teddy Baldwin.

events.label: The boarding-house keeper says Teddy Baldwin is a boss of Scowrers

communicates.speaker: boarding_house_keeper
communicates.content: He is a boss of Scowrers.

events.label: The boarding-house keeper says the Scowrers are the Eminent Order of Freemen

communicates.speaker: boarding_house_keeper
communicates.content: The Scowrers are the Eminent Order of Freemen!

events.label: McMurdo responds that he is a member of that order himself

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Why, I am a member of that order myself.

events.label: The boarding-house keeper refuses to have McMurdo in his house after learning of membership

communicates.speaker: boarding_house_keeper
communicates.content: I vould never have had you in my house if I had known it—not if you vere to pay me a hundred dollar a veek.

events.label: The boarding-house keeper says the order is a murder society

communicates.speaker: boarding_house_keeper
communicates.content: It’s a murder society, that’s vat it is.

events.label: McMurdo demands proof or an apology and threatens to leave the room

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I want you to take back what you’ve said, or else make it good. One or the other you must do before I quit this room... I guess you owe me either an apology or else an explanation, Mr. Shafter.

events.label: The boarding-house keeper says if you offend one, the other strikes you

communicates.speaker: boarding_house_keeper
communicates.content: The bosses of the one are the bosses of the other. If you offend the one, it is the other vat vill strike you. We have proved it too often.

events.label: The boarding-house keeper sentences McMurdo to leave and forbids him to sleep in the house that night

communicates.speaker: boarding_house_keeper
communicates.content: But you vill find other lodgings, mister... Yes, indeed, you shall not sleep here after to-night!

events.label: McMurdo is banished from his comfortable quarters and from the girl he loves
McMurdo finds Ettie alone in the sitting-room and tells her about receiving notice

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Sure, your father is after giving me notice,

events.label: McMurdo tells Ettie he cannot live without her

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: It’s little I would care if it was just my room, but indeed, Ettie, though it’s only a week that I’ve known you, you are the very breath of life to me, and I can’t live without you!

events.label: Ettie tells McMurdo he is too late and says she will not promise anyone else marriage

communicates.speaker: ettie
communicates.content: I have told you, have I not, that you are too late? There is another, and if I have not promised to marry him at once, at least I can promise no one else.

events.label: McMurdo kneels before Ettie and urges her not to ruin their lives over the promise

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: For God’s sake, Ettie, let it stand at that! Will you ruin your life and my own for the sake of this promise?

events.label: McMurdo seizes Ettie’s white hand and asks her to say she will be his

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Say that you will be mine, and we will face it out together!

events.label: McMurdo embraces Ettie and insists they will face the situation together in the house

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: No, here... I’ll hold you against the world, Ettie, right here where we are!

events.label: McMurdo and Ettie discuss fear of Baldwin and Scowrers and Ettie states that no witness dares to appear

communicates.speaker: ettie
communicates.content: Because no witness dares to appear against them. He would not live a month if he did. Also because they have always their own men to swear that the accused one was far from the scene of the crime.

events.label: Door opens and Teddy Baldwin enters the room
Ettie greets Teddy Baldwin

communicates.speaker: ettie
communicates.content: I’m glad to see you, Mr. Baldwin

events.label: Teddy Baldwin asks who the other man is

communicates.speaker: teddy_baldwin
communicates.content: Who is this?

events.label: Ettie introduces McMurdo as a new boarder to Teddy Baldwin

communicates.speaker: ettie
communicates.content: It’s a friend of mine, Mr. Baldwin, a new boarder here. Mr. McMurdo, may I introduce you to Mr. Baldwin?

events.label: Teddy Baldwin states Ettie is his and orders a walk

communicates.speaker: teddy_baldwin
communicates.content: this young lady is mine, and you’ll find it a very fine evening for a walk.

events.label: McMurdo refuses to go for a walk

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Thank you, I am in no humour for a walk.

events.label: Teddy Baldwin challenges McMurdo to a fight

communicates.speaker: teddy_baldwin
communicates.content: Maybe you are in a humour for a fight, Mr. Boarder!

events.label: McMurdo agrees to fight and springs to his feet

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: That I am!

events.label: McMurdo challenges Teddy Baldwin to settle matters by going to fight

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I think, Ettie, that if you were to leave us alone we could get this thing settled. Or maybe, Mr. Baldwin, you will take a turn down the street with me.

events.label: Teddy Baldwin rolls up his sleeve and shows a branded sign on his forearm
Teddy Baldwin explains he will tell McMurdo what the sign means and demands punishment for sowing

communicates.speaker: teddy_baldwin
communicates.content: D’you know what that means?... —on your knees—and then I’ll tell you what your punishment may be. You’ve sowed—and by the Lord, I’ll see that you reap!

events.label: Teddy Baldwin storms out and the outer door bangs behind him
Ettie urges McMurdo to flee tonight and says Baldwin will have his life

communicates.speaker: ettie
communicates.content: Oh, Jack, how brave you were!... But it is no use, you must fly! To-night—Jack—to-night! It’s your only hope. He will have your life.

events.label: McMurdo tells Ettie he is a Freeman and says he will tell her father about it

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: There, acushla, there! Don’t be disturbed or fear for me. I’m a Freeman myself. I’m after telling your father about it.

events.label: McMurdo says he will go make a friend of Boss McGinty and sleep elsewhere

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’ll go right now and fix it. You can tell your father that I’ll sleep here to-night and find some other quarters in the morning.

events.label: McMurdo pushes open the swinging door of McGinty’s saloon and moves into the crowd inside
McMurdo elbows his way forward toward McGinty and pushes through a small group of courtiers
McMurdo and McGinty converse about McMurdo’s identity

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Well, young man, I can’t call your face to mind.

events.label: A voice from the group identifies McGinty as Councillor McGinty

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: He’s Councillor McGinty, young man,

events.label: McMurdo says he was advised to see McGinty

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: But I was advised to see you.

events.label: McGinty asks what McMurdo thinks of him, and McMurdo responds

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: What d’you think of me?

events.label: The saloon-keeper reacts to McMurdo’s Irish speech

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: you’ve got an Irish tongue in your head anyhow

events.label: McGinty questions McMurdo’s request and orders him behind the bar

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Come in here for a moment, behind the bar.

events.label: McGinty closes the door and seats himself on barrels in the small room behind the bar
McGinty produces a revolver and warns McMurdo about playing games

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: See here, my joker, if I thought you were playing any game on us, it would be short work for you.

events.label: McMurdo and McGinty conduct an exchange about lodge membership and identities

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Lodge 29, Chicago.

events.label: McGinty asks McMurdo where he is doing work and McMurdo states he is working

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Working, the same as you—but a poorer job.

events.label: McGinty questions McMurdo about hearing anything of the lodge and McMurdo responds

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’ve heard that it takes a man to be a brother.

events.label: McMurdo refuses to explain why he left Chicago

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’m damned if I tell you that!

events.label: McMurdo shows McGinty a newspaper cutting
McGinty reads the newspaper cutting about the shooting of Jonas Pinto
McGinty asks whether McMurdo was responsible for the shooting and McMurdo confirms

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Your work?

events.label: McMurdo explains he shot Jonas Pinto during coin-related crime and then went to coal country

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I just killed him and lighted out for the coal country.

events.label: McGinty inspects dollars shown by McMurdo and McGinty states he can see no difference

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: I can see no difference.

events.label: McMurdo draws a cocked pistol and says he was covering McGinty

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I was covering you all the time.

events.label: The bartender is told to report that Ted Baldwin must see Councillor McGinty immediately

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: I’m sorry, Councillor, but it’s Ted Baldwin. He says he must see you this very minute.

events.label: McGinty pushes the bartender out and closes the door on him
McGinty confronts McMurdo and says he has a word to say about him

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: I’ve a word to say to you, Councillor, about this man.

events.label: McGinty tells Baldwin not to greet the new brother in that fashion and orders Baldwin to make it up

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Hold out your hand, man, and make it up!

events.label: McMurdo offers to fight Baldwin and leaves the decision between them to McGinty as Bodymaster

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’ll fight him with fists, or, if that won’t satisfy him, I’ll fight him any other way he chooses.

events.label: McGinty states there is a young lady dispute and rules she is free to choose between the brothers of the lodge

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: A young lady.

events.label: McGinty and Baldwin argue about rulings, then McGinty assaults Baldwin by grabbing his neck and hurling him across barrels
McMurdo intervenes to stop McGinty from squeezing Baldwin to death

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Easy, Councillor!

events.label: McGinty and Baldwin resume cordial relations and McGinty starts a champagne toast to end quarrelling
McGinty states that after the toast there can be no bad blood and that they will come under lodge discipline if it goes further

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: That’s the end of the black blood.

events.label: McGinty tells McMurdo and Baldwin to be affiliated to Lodge 341, Vermissa, and invites them to Saturday night’s meeting

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: You’ll have to be affiliated to Lodge 341, Brother McMurdo.

events.label: The following day, McMurdo moves his lodgings from old Jacob Shafter’s to the Widow MacNamara’s
Scanlan moves into Vermissa and lodges together with McMurdo
McMurdo takes out coining moulds in his bedroom at his new abode
McMurdo allows brothers from the lodge to come in and view the coining moulds and take examples of false money
McMurdo goes to McGinty’s saloon in the evenings to make closer acquaintance with the gang known as 'the boys'
A man enters McGinty’s saloon wearing mine police uniform and peaked cap and enrolls among McGinty’s customers
The mine police captain orders a straight whisky and asks if he has met McGinty before

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: A straight whisky; for the night is bitter,

events.label: McGinty asks whether the new police captain is Captain Marvin

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: You’ll be the new captain?

events.label: Captain Marvin says his name is Captain Marvin and tells McGinty that law and order needs help in the township

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Captain Marvin is my name.

events.label: McGinty tells Captain Marvin to do without him

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: We’d do better without you, Captain Marvin, for we have our own police of the township, and no need for any imported goods.

events.label: McGinty accuses Captain Marvin of being hired to club or shoot poorer citizens

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: What are you but the paid tool of the capitalists, hired by them to club or shoot your poorer fellow citizen?

events.label: A police officer responds good-humouredly to an argument

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Well, well, we won’t argue about that

events.label: The police officer says duty cannot be seen the same

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: I expect we all do our duty same as we see it; but we can’t all see it the same.

events.label: A police officer turns and looks at Jack McMurdo
The police officer calls out Hullo twice to Jack McMurdo

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Hullo! Hullo!

events.label: The police officer identifies Jack McMurdo as an old acquaintance

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Here’s an old acquaintance!

events.label: McMurdo moves away from the police officer
Jack McMurdo says he was never a friend to the police

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I was never a friend to you nor any other cursed copper in my life

events.label: The police captain says an acquaintance isn’t always a friend

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: An acquaintance isn’t always a friend,

events.label: The police captain asserts McMurdo is Jack McMurdo of Chicago

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: You’re Jack McMurdo of Chicago, right enough, and don’t you deny it!

events.label: McMurdo shrugs his shoulders
McMurdo says he is not denying his identity

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’m not denying it,

events.label: McMurdo asks if he should be ashamed of his own name

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: D’ye think I’m ashamed of my own name?

events.label: The police captain says McMurdo has good cause to be ashamed

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: You’ve got good cause to be, anyhow.

events.label: McMurdo asks what the police captain means

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: What the devil d’you mean by that?

events.label: McMurdo roars with fists clenched
McMurdo is warned not to bluster; the police captain claims Chicago service

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: No, no, Jack, bluster won’t do with me. I was an officer in Chicago before ever I came to this darned coal bunker, and I know a Chicago crook when I see one.

events.label: McMurdo's face falls
McMurdo asks if Captain Marvin is the Chicago Central 'Teddy Marvin'

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Don’t tell me that you’re Marvin of the Chicago Central!

events.label: Captain Marvin states he is Teddy Marvin

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Just the same old Teddy Marvin, at your service.

events.label: Captain Marvin references the shooting of Jonas Pinto

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: We haven’t forgotten the shooting of Jonas Pinto up there.

events.label: McMurdo says he never shot Jonas Pinto

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I never shot him.

events.label: Captain Marvin asserts Did you not and calls evidence impartial

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Did you not? That’s good impartial evidence, ain’t it?

events.label: Captain Marvin says Jonas Pinto's death was handy for McMurdo

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Well, his death came in uncommon handy for you, or they would have had you for shoving the queer.

events.label: Captain Marvin claims no clear case exists and says Chicago is open to McMurdo tomorrow

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Well, we can let that be bygones; for, between you and me—and perhaps I’m going further than my duty in saying it—they could get no clear case against you, and Chicago’s open to you to-morrow.

events.label: McMurdo says he is very well where he is

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’m very well where I am.

events.label: Captain Marvin says McMurdo should thank him for a pointer

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Well, I’ve given you the pointer, and you’re a sulky dog not to thank me for it.

events.label: McMurdo thanks Captain Marvin in a no very gracious manner

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, I suppose you mean well, and I do thank you,

events.label: Captain Marvin says it’s mum with him if McMurdo lives straight

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: It’s mum with me so long as I see you living on the straight,

events.label: Captain Marvin warns that if McMurdo gets off after this it is another story

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: But, by the Lord! if you get off after this, it’s another story!

events.label: Captain Marvin says good-night to McMurdo and to Councillor

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: So good-night to you—and good-night, Councillor.

events.label: Captain Marvin leaves the bar-room after creating a local hero
McMurdo becomes free of the community from that time on
McMurdo is introduced to the lodge on a Saturday night
Members gather in a large room reserved at the Union House for the assembly
McGinty sits at the head of the assembly wearing a flat black velvet cap and purple stole
McMurdo is led into an outer room by two solemn brothers
An inner guard enters with a green and gold sash across the chest and announces an order

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: The Bodymaster orders that he shall be trussed, blinded, and entered

events.label: Three men remove McMurdo's coat, turn up his right sleeve, and bind a rope above his elbows
The men place a thick black cap over McMurdo's head and upper face
McMurdo is led into the assembly hall
The voice asks McMurdo if he is already a member of the Ancient Order of Freemen

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: John McMurdo, are you already a member of the Ancient Order of Freemen?

events.label: McMurdo bows in assent to being a member
The voice asks if McMurdo is from lodge No. 29, Chicago

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: Is your lodge No. 29, Chicago?

events.label: McMurdo bows again
The voice and McMurdo exchange comments about dark nights and heavy clouds

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: Dark nights are unpleasant. (McMurdo answers) Yes, for strangers to travel. (Then) The clouds are heavy.

events.label: The voice and McMurdo exchange a response about a storm approaching and whether brethren are satisfied

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: Yes, a storm is approaching. Are the brethren satisfied?

events.label: There is a general murmur of assent
McGinty says the brethren know McMurdo is one of them by sign and countersign

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: We know, Brother, by your sign and by your countersign that you are indeed one of us,

events.label: McGinty asks if McMurdo is ready to be tested and McMurdo answers yes

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Are you ready to be tested? I am.

events.label: McGinty asks if McMurdo is of stout heart and McMurdo answers yes

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Are you of stout heart? I am.

events.label: McGinty orders McMurdo to take a stride forward to prove it; pressure appears then disappears

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Take a stride forward to prove it.

events.label: The voice states McMurdo is of stout heart

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: He is of stout heart,

events.label: The voice asks if McMurdo can bear pain; McMurdo answers yes

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: Can you bear pain? As well as another,

events.label: The voice orders the test; agonizing pain shoots through McMurdo's forearm

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: Test him!

events.label: McMurdo nearly screams out but bites his lip and clenches his hands
McMurdo says he can take more than that

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I can take more than that,

events.label: The hood is plucked from McMurdo's head and he stands blinking and smiling amid congratulations
McGinty confirms McMurdo has sworn secrecy and asks if he accepts the Bodymaster's rule; McMurdo answers yes

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: You have already sworn the oath of secrecy and fidelity, and you are aware that the punishment for any breach of it is instant and inevitable death? I am. And you accept the rule of the Bodymaster for the time being under all circumstances? I do.

events.label: McGinty welcomes McMurdo to Lodge 341 privileges and orders Scanlan to put liquor on the table

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Then in the name of Lodge 341, Vermissa, I welcome you to its privileges and debates. You will put the liquor on the table, Brother Scanlan, and we will drink to our worthy brother.

events.label: A branding mark is visible on McMurdo's forearm
McMurdo listens to the lodge business with open ears and surprise
McGinty reads a letter from Division Master Windle of Merton County Lodge 249 to the lodge

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: There is a job to be done on Andrew Rae... You will send two good men... He will show them when to act and where... Yours in freedom, 'J.W. WINDLE, D.M.A.O.F.'

events.label: McGinty asks for volunteers; Tiger Cormac is selected and Wilson is called

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Who will volunteer for the job? You’ll do, Tiger Cormac. If you handle it as well as you did the last, you won’t be wrong. And you, Wilson.

events.label: Wilson says he has no pistol; McGinty responds about it being provided and timing on Monday

communicates.speaker: wilson
communicates.content: I’ve no pistol

events.label: Cormac is asked about any reward; McGinty says honour is required and odd dollars may follow

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Never mind the reward. You just do it for the honour of the thing. Maybe when it is done there will be a few odd dollars at the bottom of the box.

events.label: McGinty refuses to explain the target's deeds and says they will carry it out as for others

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Sure, it’s not for the likes of you to ask what the man has done. He has been judged over there... All we have to do is to carry it out for them, same as they would for us.

events.label: Ted Baldwin complains three men were turned off by Foreman Blaker

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: It was only last week that three of our men were turned off by Foreman Blaker.

events.label: A man laughs and mentions the business end of a buckshot cartridge

communicates.speaker: anonymous_lodge_man
communicates.content: The business end of a buckshot cartridge!

events.label: McMurdo rises and offers to help; the chairman asks him to wait

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I would say, Eminent Bodymaster, that if a man should be wanted I should take it as an honour to be chosen to help the lodge.

events.label: The chairman tells McMurdo they have marked him down and discusses a pension for Jim Carnaway's widow

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: We have marked you down as a willing man... There is a small matter to-night... First of all, I will ask the treasurer as to our bank balance. There is the pension to Jim Carnaway’s widow. He was struck down doing the work of the lodge, and it is for us to see that she is not the loser.

events.label: McMurdo's neighbour says Jim was shot while trying to kill Chester Wilcox of Marley Creek

communicates.speaker: anonymous_neighbor
communicates.content: Jim was shot last month when they tried to kill Chester Wilcox of Marley Creek,

events.label: The treasurer states funds are good and recounts payments and threats

communicates.speaker: treasurer_higgins
communicates.content: The funds are good at the moment... Max Linder & Co. paid five hundred to be left alone. Walker Brothers sent in a hundred; but I took it on myself to return it and ask for five... Then the West Section Coaling Company has paid its annual contribution. We have enough on hand to meet any obligations.

events.label: A brother asks about Archie Swindon; the treasurer says he sold out and left the district

communicates.speaker: treasurer_higgins
communicates.content: He has sold out and left the district... I guess he won’t show his face in this valley again.

events.label: Mr. Morris asks who bought driven-out property; treasurer answers it was bought by the State & Merton County Railroad Company

communicates.speaker: treasurer_higgins
communicates.content: It has been bought by the State & Merton County Railroad Company.

events.label: Mr. Morris asks who bought Todman and Lee mines; treasurer answers the same company

communicates.speaker: treasurer_higgins
communicates.content: The same company... They were all bought by the West Gilmerton General Mining Company.

events.label: Mr. Morris argues big companies can hunt them down and bring them to court

communicates.speaker: mc_morris
communicates.content: This process has been going on now for ten long years... We find in their places great companies... We can take it out of their local bosses; but it only means that others will be sent in their stead... So long as we did not squeeze them too dry, they would stay on under our power. But if these big companies find that we stand between them and their profits, they will spare no pains and no expense to hunt us down and bring us to court.

events.label: A hush occurs and faces darken as gloomy looks are exchanged

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: None

events.label: A speaker advises going easier upon the small men

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: It is my advice that we go easier upon the small men.

events.label: A speaker states that driving the small men out will break the power of the society

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: On the day that they have all been driven out the power of this society will have been broken.

events.label: Angry cries occur as the speaker resumes his seat
McGinty rises with gloom on his brow
McGinty addresses Brother Morris and calls him a croaker

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Brother Morris, you were always a croaker.

events.label: McGinty claims the lodge members standing together cannot be touched by any power in the United States

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: So long as the members of this lodge stand together there is no power in the United States that can touch them.

events.label: McGinty asks whether they have not tried it often enough in the law courts

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Sure, have we not tried it often enough in the lawcourts?

events.label: McGinty states big companies will find it easier to pay than to fight

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: I expect the big companies will find it easier to pay than to fight, same as the little companies do.

events.label: McGinty announces the lodge has finished its business for the evening except one small matter

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: And now, Brethren, this lodge has finished its business for the evening, save for one small matter which may be mentioned when we are parting.

events.label: McGinty states it is time for fraternal refreshment and harmony

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: The time has now come for fraternal refreshment and for harmony.

events.label: McMurdo is described as thrilling the lodge with specific songs
A new recruit becomes popular and is marked for advancement and high office
The whisky bottle passes around and men become flushed and ripe for mischief
Bodymaster tells the boys that one man in town wants trimming up

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: Boys, there's one man in this town that wants trimming up, and it's for you to see that he gets it.

events.label: Bodymaster identifies the target as James Stanger of the Herald

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: I'm speaking of James Stanger of the Herald.

events.label: Bodymaster asks if they have seen how Stanger has been opening his mouth against them

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: You've seen how he's been opening his mouth against us again?

events.label: Assent murmurs with muttered oaths occur
McGinty takes a slip of paper from his waistcoat pocket
The chairman tosses the paper down upon the table
Multiple voices cry that James Stanger should be killed
Brother Morris protests against killing James Stanger

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I protest against that.

events.label: Brother Morris warns the group is too heavy in the valley and self-defense will crush them

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I tell you, Brethren, that our hand is too heavy in this valley, and that there will come a point where in self-defense every man will unite to crush us out.

events.label: Brother Morris states James Stanger is an old man

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: James Stanger is an old man.

events.label: McGinty asks how they would bring about the group’s destruction

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: And how would they bring about our destruction, Mr. Standback?

events.label: McGinty questions whether police would bring destruction and says half are in their pay and half afraid

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Is it by the police? Sure, half of them are in our pay and half of them afraid of us.

events.label: McGinty questions whether law courts and a judge would bring destruction and asks what happened when they tried before

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Or is it by the law courts and the judge? Haven’t we tried that before now, and what ever came of it?

events.label: Brother Morris suggests a Judge Lynch might try the case

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: There is a Judge Lynch that might try the case.

events.label: A general shout of anger occurs in response to the suggestion
McGinty states he can put two hundred men into town to clear it out end to end

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: I have but to raise my finger, and I could put two hundred men into this town that would clear it out from end to end.

events.label: McGinty warns Brother Morris he is watched and threatens to place Morris’s name on the agenda paper

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: See here, Brother Morris, I have my eye on you, and have had for some time! You’ve no heart yourself, and you try to take the heart out of others. It will be an ill day for you, Brother Morris, when your own name comes on our agenda paper, and I’m thinking that it’s just there that I ought to place it.

events.label: Brother Morris turns deadly pale and falls back into his chair
Brother Morris raises his glass in a trembling hand and drinks before answering
Brother Morris apologizes to the Eminent Bodymaster and the brothers for speaking more than he should

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I apologize, Eminent Bodymaster, to you and to every brother in this lodge if I have said more than I should.

events.label: Brother Morris says he is a faithful member and fears evil coming to the lodge

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I am a faithful member—you all know that—and it is my fear lest evil come to the lodge which makes me speak in anxious words.

events.label: Brother Morris promises he will not offend again

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: But I have greater trust in your judgment than in my own, Eminent Bodymaster, and I promise you that I will not offend again.

events.label: The Bodymaster’s scowl relaxes as he listens to Brother Morris
Bodymaster tells Brother Morris it is very good

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: Very good, Brother Morris.

events.label: Bodymaster states the lodge will be united in word and deed while he is in the chair

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: But so long as I am in this chair we shall be a united lodge in word and in deed.

events.label: Bodymaster says if Stanger got his full deserts there would be more trouble and that editors hang together

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: And now, boys, I'll say this much, that if Stanger got his full deserts there would be more trouble than we need ask for. These editors hang together, and every journal in the state would be crying out for police and troops.

events.label: Bodymaster says they can give Stanger a pretty severe warning

communicates.speaker: bodymaster
communicates.content: But I guess you can give him a pretty severe warning.

events.label: Bodymaster asks Brother Baldwin to fix it
Brother Baldwin agrees

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: Sure!

events.label: Brother Baldwin says how many will be taken

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: How many will you take?

events.label: Brother Baldwin states half a dozen plus two to guard the door, then names men

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: Half a dozen, and two to guard the door. You'll come, Gower, and you, Mansel, and you, Scanlan, and the two Willabys.

events.label: The chairman says he promised the new brother he should go

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: I promised the new brother he should go.

events.label: Ted Baldwin looks at McMurdo with eyes that show he has not forgotten or forgiven
Ted Baldwin orders them to get to work soon

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: That's enough. The sooner we get to work the better.

events.label: The company breaks up with shouts, yells, and drunken song

The men stop and gather in a yard facing a high building
Baldwin instructs McMurdo to stand below at the door and keep the road open

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: Here, you, said Baldwin to McMurdo, you can stand below at the door and see that the road is kept open for us.

events.label: Baldwin tells the others to come with him

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: You others come with me.

events.label: Baldwin tells them to have no fears, claiming they have witnesses in the Union Bar

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: Have no fears, boys; for we have a dozen witnesses that we are in the Union Bar at this very moment.

events.label: Baldwin and his men rush into the newspaper office and up the stair
McMurdo and another remain below

There is a thud as sticks clatter and the man is struck down
Baldwin hacks at the man’s head while the victim tries to defend with his arms
McMurdo dashes up and pushes Baldwin back
McMurdo says Baldwin will kill the man

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: You’ll kill the man.

events.label: McMurdo orders Baldwin to drop it

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Drop it!

events.label: Baldwin accuses McMurdo of interfering and tells him to stand back

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: Who are you to interfere—you that are new to the lodge? Stand back!

events.label: McMurdo whips out a pistol
McMurdo orders Baldwin to stand back himself

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Stand back yourself!

events.label: McMurdo threatens to blow Baldwin’s face in if he lays a hand on him

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’ll blow your face in if you lay a hand on me.

events.label: McMurdo cites Bodymaster’s order that the man was not to be killed and accuses Baldwin of killing him

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: As to the lodge, wasn’t it the order of the Bodymaster that the man was not to be killed—and what are you doing but killing him?

events.label: A man remarks that what McMurdo says is truth

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: It’s truth he says.

events.label: A man below urges them to hurry because the windows are lighting up

communicates.speaker: gower
communicates.content: By Gar! you’d best hurry yourselves!

events.label: A man below says the whole town will arrive inside five minutes

communicates.speaker: gower
communicates.content: The windows are all lighting up, and you’ll have the whole town here inside of five minutes.

events.label: A group of compositors and pressmen forms in the hall below
Criminals leave the editor’s body at the stair head and rush down
Some criminals mix with the crowd in McGinty’s saloon and whisper that the job was carried through

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: the job had been well carried through

events.label: Others, including McMurdo, leave into side streets and go to their homes by devious paths
McMurdo awakes next morning
McMurdo reads the Daily Herald
In a special column, a headline reads 'Outrage at the Herald Office—Editor Seriously Injured'
The newspaper statement says the matter is in police hands and hopes of better results are unlikely
The newspaper states there is no immediate danger to Stanger’s life
The newspaper states a guard of police armed with Winchester rifles was requisitioned to defend the office
A knock occurs and McMurdo’s landlady brings him an unsigned note
McMurdo receives a note that directs him to speak by the flagstaff upon Miller Hill

communicates.speaker: note_3143
communicates.content: I should wish to speak to you, but would rather not do so in your house. You will find me beside the flagstaff upon Miller Hill. If you will come there now, I have something which it is important for you to hear and for me to say.

events.label: McMurdo decides to see the matter through and goes to Miller Hill
McMurdo sees Brother Morris beside the flagstaff when Morris turns his face
The lodge sign is given and exchanged as McMurdo and Brother Morris meet
Brother Morris tells McMurdo he wanted to have a word with him

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I wanted to have a word with you, Mr. McMurdo.

events.label: McMurdo asks why Morris did not put his name to the note

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Why did you not put your name to the note?

events.label: Morris says one has to be cautious and never knows who to trust or not to trust

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: One has to be cautious, mister. One never knows in times like these how a thing may come back to one. One never knows either who to trust or who not to trust.

events.label: McMurdo says he may trust brothers of the lodge

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Surely one may trust brothers of the lodge.

events.label: Morris denies it and says whatever they say or think goes back to McGinty

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: No, no, not always. Whatever we say, even what we think, seems to go back to that man McGinty.

events.label: Morris says McMurdo swore good faith to the Bodymaster and asks whether Morris would ask him to break his oath

events.label: Morris says it is sorry he gave McMurdo the trouble and that two free citizens cannot speak their thoughts

communicates.content: If that is the view you take, I can only say that I am sorry I gave you the trouble to come and meet me. Things have come to a bad pass when two free citizens cannot speak their thoughts to each other.

events.label: McMurdo says he is loyal to the lodge and will not repeat what Morris says in confidence

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: For myself I am loyal to the lodge, and so I tell you straight; but I would be a poor creature if I were to repeat to any other what you might say to me in confidence.

events.label: McMurdo warns Morris he may get neither help nor sympathy

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: It will go no further than me; though I warn you that you may get neither help nor sympathy.

events.label: Morris asks McMurdo whether joining the Freeman’s society in Chicago led him to crime

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: If you give me away, may a curse be on you! ... when you joined the Freeman’s society in Chicago and swore vows of charity and fidelity, did ever it cross your mind that you might find it would lead you to crime?

events.label: Morris insists it is crime

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: Call it crime!

events.label: Morris denies having thought of a thing when he joined the Freeman’s society

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: No, I’m bound to say I did not.

events.label: Morris says he joined at Philadelphia and describes it as a benefit club and meeting place

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: Nor did I when I joined it at Philadelphia. It was just a benefit club and a meeting place for one’s fellows.

events.label: Morris says his wife and three children came with him

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: My wife and three children came with me.

events.label: Morris starts a drygoods store on Market Square and prospered
