communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: The word had gone round that I was a Freeman, and I was forced to join the local lodge, same as you did last night.

events.label: Morris shows having a badge of shame on his forearm and branding on his heart

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I’ve the badge of shame on my forearm and something worse branded on my heart.

events.label: Morris says he was under orders of a black villain and caught in a meshwork of crime

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I found that I was under the orders of a black villain and caught in a meshwork of crime.

events.label: Morris says every word he said to make things better was taken as treason

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: Every word I said to make things better was taken as treason, same as it was last night.

events.label: Morris says he cannot get away because all he has in the world is in his store

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I can’t get away; for all I have in the world is in my store.

events.label: Morris says leaving the society would mean murder for him and consequences for his wife and children

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: If I leave the society, I know well that it means murder to me, and God knows what to my wife and children.

events.label: Morris describes a lonely house 20 miles away and says others went in while he was kept at the door

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: It was a lonely house, twenty miles from here, over the range yonder. I was told off for the door, same as you were last night. They could not trust me with the job. The others went in.

events.label: Morris says when the others came out their hands were crimson to the wrists

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: When they came out their hands were crimson to the wrists.

events.label: Morris says a child screamed from the house and identifies it as a five-year-old boy who saw his father murdered

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: As we turned away a child was screaming out of the house behind us. It was a boy of five who had seen his father murdered.

events.label: Morris says he was a criminal, part sharer in a murder, and that a priest had no word with him because he was a Scowrer

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: But I was a criminal then, part sharer in a murder, lost forever in this world, and lost also in the next. I am a good Catholic; but the priest would have no word with me when he heard I was a Scowrer, and I am excommunicated from my faith.

events.label: Morris asks McMurdo whether he is ready to be a cold-blooded murderer and asks what end can be done to stop it

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: And I see you going down the same road, and I ask you what the end is to be. Are you ready to be a cold-blooded murderer also, or can we do anything to stop it?

events.label: McMurdo asks what Morris would do

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: What would you do?

events.label: McMurdo asks whether Morris would inform

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: You would not inform?

events.label: Morris replies that God forbids and says the thought would cost his life

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: God forbid! Sure, the very thought would cost me my life.

events.label: McMurdo tells Morris he will let him know what he thinks after seeing more

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, I’ll let you know what I think when I have seen more,

events.label: McMurdo is offered a clerkship by Morris and refuses it

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I offer you a clerkship in my store.

events.label: McMurdo refuses Morris’s clerkship offer

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: And I refuse it.

events.label: Morris warns McMurdo they may have been seen together and says someone may ask what they spoke about

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: One word before you go. We may have been seen together. They may want to know what we have spoken about.

events.label: McMurdo receives a visit from Boss McGinty who enters his sitting-room the same afternoon
McGinty questions McMurdo about the arm and about what was spoken with Morris on Miller Hill

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: How’s the arm?

events.label: McGinty asks what McMurdo was speaking about on Miller Hill this morning

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: What were you speaking to Brother Morris about on Miller Hill this morning?

events.label: McMurdo laughs and reports Morris offered him a clerkship in a drygoods store, which Morris suggested after thinking McMurdo was idle

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Morris didn’t know I could earn a living here at home. He shan’t know either; for he has got too much conscience for the likes of me. But he’s a good-hearted old chap. It was his idea that I was at a loose end, and that he would do me a good turn by offering me a clerkship in a drygoods store.

events.label: McMurdo says he refused the clerkship because he can earn more in his own bedroom

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Sure. Couldn’t I earn ten times as much in my own bedroom with four hours’ work?

events.label: McGinty says there is no room for scabby sheep in their pen and warns McMurdo about keeping company with a disloyal man

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: There’s no room for scabby sheep in our pen. But if you keep company with a disloyal man, we might think that you were disloyal, too.

events.label: Police force enters the room with rifles leveled at McMurdo
Captain Marvin enters and orders McMurdo to take his hat and come along with police

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Take your hat and come along with us.

events.label: Captain Marvin states McMurdo is being taken because of trouble and addresses him as Mr. Crooked McMurdo of Chicago

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: I thought you’d be getting into trouble, Mr. Crooked McMurdo of Chicago

events.label: Captain Marvin says they are not out after McGinty but after McMurdo and that McGinty should help rather than hinder

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: You’re standing out in this deal, Councillor McGinty. We are not out after you, but after this man McMurdo. It is for you to help, not to hinder us in our duty.

events.label: Captain Marvin orders Patrolman to cover McMurdo while he disarms him
McMurdo asserts he has a pistol

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: There’s my pistol

events.label: Captain Marvin accuses McMurdo of being concerned in the beating of old Editor Stanger

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Of being concerned in the beating of old Editor Stanger at the Herald office. It wasn’t your fault that it isn’t a murder charge.

events.label: McGinty claims he can provide witnesses that McMurdo was playing poker with him in his saloon up to midnight

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: This man was with me in my saloon playing poker up to midnight, and I can bring a dozen to prove it.

events.label: Captain Marvin orders McMurdo to come quietly and threatens to place a gun across McMurdo’s head if he does not

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Meanwhile, come on, McMurdo, and come quietly if you don’t want a gun across your head. You stand wide, Mr. McGinty; for I warn you I will stand no resistance when I am on duty!

events.label: McGinty searches the house and finds no trace of a concealed coining plant
Captain Marvin and his men escort McMurdo to police headquarters after arrest
McMurdo is pushed into the police station and placed in the common cell
McMurdo is found in a cell with Baldwin and three other criminals
A jailer gives bedding and bottles of whisky and a pack of cards to prisoners late at night
The accused prisoners are discharged after a magistrate decision based on evidence
A little, dark-bearded resolute fellow addresses the ex-prisoners and calls them damned murderers

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: You damned murderers!

events.label: Jack says to the woman that it is her

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: It’s you!

events.label: Jack says he is mopping his brow

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: said he, mopping his brow.

events.label: Jack claims the woman came to him and he could only want to strangle her

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: And to think that you should come to me, heart of my heart, and I should find nothing better to do than to want to strangle you!

events.label: Jack holds out his arms and asks the woman to come to him

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Come then, darling, let me make it up to you.

events.label: The woman does not recover from a glimpse of guilty fear in the man’s face
The woman asks Jack what has come over him

communicates.speaker: woman
communicates.content: What’s come over you, Jack?

events.label: The woman asks why Jack was scared of her and claims he would not look at her that way if his conscience were at ease

communicates.speaker: woman
communicates.content: Why were you so scared of me? Oh, Jack, if your conscience was at ease, you would not have looked at me like that!

events.label: Jack says he was thinking of other things when the woman came tripping lightly

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Sure, I was thinking of other things, and when you came tripping so lightly on those fairy feet of yours—

events.label: Jack says it was more than that

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: No, no, it was more than that, Jack.

events.label: The woman suspects something and asks to see the letter Jack was writing

communicates.speaker: woman
communicates.content: Let me see that letter you were writing.

events.label: Jack refuses to let the woman see the letter

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Ah, Ettie, I couldn’t do that.

events.label: The woman claims the letter is to another woman

communicates.speaker: woman
communicates.content: It’s to another woman,

events.label: The woman accuses Jack of writing to his wife and says she does not know he is married or unmarried

communicates.speaker: woman
communicates.content: I know it! Why else should you hold it from me? Was it to your wife that you were writing? How am I to know that you are not a married man—you, a stranger, that nobody knows?

events.label: Jack says he is not married and swears the woman is the only one he has

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: I am not married, Ettie. See now, I swear it! You’re the only one woman on earth to me. By the cross of Christ I swear it!

events.label: The woman asks why Jack will not show her the letter

communicates.speaker: woman
communicates.content: Well, then, why will you not show me the letter?

events.label: Jack says he is under oath not to show the letter, that it is secret due to the lodge, and that he might fear a detective

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: I’ll tell you, acushla. I’m under oath not to show it, and just as I wouldn’t break my word to you so I would keep it to those who hold my promise. It’s the business of the lodge, and even to you it’s secret. And if I was scared when a hand fell on me, can’t you understand it when it might have been the hand of a detective?

events.label: Jack gathers the woman into his arms and kisses away her fears and doubts
Jack tells the woman to sit by him and asks whether her mind is easy again

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Sit here by me, then. It’s a queer throne for such a queen; but it’s the best your poor lover can find. He’ll do better for you some of these days, I’m thinking. Now your mind is easy once again, is it not?

events.label: The woman says Jack cannot be at ease and references murder court fears and the nickname "McMurdo the Scowrer"

communicates.speaker: woman
communicates.content: How can it ever be at ease, Jack, when I know that you are a criminal among criminals, when I never know the day that I may hear you are in court for murder? ‘McMurdo the Scowrer,’ that’s what one of our boarders called you yesterday. It went through my heart like a knife.

events.label: Jack says hard words break no bones and that they were true

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Sure, hard words break no bones. But they were true.

events.label: Jack says it is not so bad and that poor men try to get their rights

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Well, dear, it’s not so bad as you think. We are but poor men that are trying in our own way to get our rights.

events.label: The woman embraces Jack and implores him to give up, kneeling to ask for it

communicates.speaker: woman
communicates.content: Give it up, Jack! For my sake, for God’s sake, give it up! It was to ask you that I came here to-day. Oh, Jack, see—I beg it of you on my bended knees! Kneeling here before you I implore you to give it up!

events.label: Jack raises the woman and soothes her with her head against his breast
Jack says he cannot give it up because it would break his oath and desert his comrades and because the lodge would not let a man go free with secrets

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Sure, my darlin’, you don’t know what it is you are asking. How could I give it up when it would be to break my oath and to desert my comrades? If you could see how things stand with me you could never ask it of me. Besides, if I wanted to, how could I do it? You don’t suppose that the lodge would let a man go free with all its secrets?

events.label: The woman proposes a plan involving saving money and fleeing to Philadelphia or New York to be safe

communicates.speaker: woman
communicates.content: I’ve thought of that, Jack. I’ve planned it all. Father has saved some money. He is weary of this place where the fear of these people darkens our lives. He is ready to go. We would fly together to Philadelphia or New York, where we would be safe from them.

events.label: Jack laughs and says the lodge has a long arm reaching Philadelphia or New York

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: The lodge has a long arm. Do you think it could not stretch from here to Philadelphia or New York?

events.label: The woman suggests going west, to England, or to Germany

communicates.speaker: woman
communicates.content: Well, then, to the West, or to England, or to Germany, where father came from—anywhere to get away from this Valley of Fear!

events.label: Jack references old Brother Morris and says the valley shadow lies heavy

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Sure, it is the second time I have heard the valley so named. The shadow does indeed seem to lie heavy on some of you.

events.label: Jack says the shadow darkens their lives and asks about Ted Baldwin being unforgiving and fearing them

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: It darkens every moment of our lives. Do you suppose that Ted Baldwin has ever forgiven us? If it were not that he fears you, what do you suppose our chances would be? If you saw the look in those dark, hungry eyes of his when they fall on me!

events.label: Jack swears he would teach Ted Baldwin manners, says he cannot leave, and says he cannot have it taken from him

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: By Gar! I’d teach him better manners if I caught him at it! But see here, little girl. I can’t leave here. I can’t—take that from me once and for all. But if you will leave me to find my own way, I will try to prepare a way of getting honourably out of it.

events.label: Jack proposes six months to prepare a way to leave, and the woman reacts with joy

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Well, well, it’s just how you look at it. But if you’ll give me six months, I’ll work it so that I can leave without being ashamed to look others in the face.

events.label: The woman asks whether it is a promise

communicates.speaker: woman
communicates.content: Is it a promise?

events.label: Jack says it may be seven or eight but within a year at the furthest they will leave the valley behind

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Well, it may be seven or eight. But within a year at the furthest we will leave the valley behind us.

events.label: The woman returns to her father’s house more light-hearted than before Jack came into her life
McMurdo is soon to discover the organization is wider and more complex than the simple lodge
An official named the County Delegate lives at Hobson’s Patch farther down the line and wields power over several lodges
McMurdo sees the County Delegate once
Evans Pott is identified as the County Delegate and Boss of Vermissa shows repulsion and fear toward him
Scanlan receives a note from McGinty enclosing one from Evans Pott about sending Lawler and Andrews

communicates.speaker: evans_pott
communicates.content: he was sending over two good men, Lawler and Andrews, who had instructions to act in the neighbourhood; though it was best for the cause that no particulars as to their objects should be given.

events.label: The note asks the Bodymaster to arrange lodgings and comfort for the strangers

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Would the Bodymaster see to it that suitable arrangements be made for their lodgings and comfort until the time for action should arrive?

events.label: McGinty adds that secrecy at the Union House is impossible and asks McMurdo and Scanlan to put the strangers up briefly

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: it was impossible for anyone to remain secret at the Union House, and that, therefore, he would be obliged if McMurdo and Scanlan would put the strangers up for a few days in their boarding house.

events.label: Lawler and Andrews arrive carrying their gripsacks
Lawler and Andrews behave as exemplary society members while being assassins
Scanlan says that everyone is in it together as the four sit at supper

communicates.speaker: scanlan
communicates.content: Sure, we are all in it together,

events.label: Scanlan says they will talk about past killings but say nothing until the work is done

communicates.speaker: scanlan
communicates.content: That’s true enough, and we’ll talk till the cows come home of the killing of Charlie Williams or of Simon Bird, or any other job in the past. But till the work is done we say nothing.

events.label: McMurdo asks whether Lawler is after Jack Knox of Ironhill and says he would go a way to see him get his deserts

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: There are half a dozen about here that I have a word to say to. I suppose it isn’t Jack Knox of Ironhill that you are after. I’d go some way to see him get his deserts.

events.label: Lawler says it is not Jack Knox

communicates.speaker: lawler
communicates.content: No, it’s not him yet.

events.label: McMurdo mentions Herman Strauss and Lawler says it is not him either

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Or Herman Strauss?

events.label: McMurdo says he cannot force answers but would be glad to know

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, if you won’t tell us we can’t make you; but I’d be glad to know.

events.label: Lawler smiles and shakes his head and is not drawn
McMurdo hears Lawler and Andrews creeping down the stairs and wakes Scanlan; both hurry to dress
McMurdo and Scanlan find that Lawler and Andrews have stolen out and left the door open behind them
McMurdo and Scanlan follow Lawler and Andrews warily through snow and meet a waiting group
The strangers take the trail to Crow Hill mine
A steam whistle screams as the signal before cages descend
A hundred miners wait at the open space round the mine shaft under the engine house shadow while it is bitterly cold
The mine engineer Menzies blows his whistle for the cages to be lowered

communicates.speaker: minzies
communicates.content: whistle for the cages to be lowered

events.label: Andrews advances eagerly toward the pit head and his eyes fall upon the silent group
Menzies asks who the intruders are and what they are loitering for; Andrews shoots him in the stomach

communicates.speaker: minzies
communicates.content: Who are you? What are you loitering there for?

events.label: The miners remain motionless as the manager is shot and goes down
Menzies roars and rushes with an iron spanner, then gets shot and drops dead
Some miners surge forward then the strangers empty six-shooters over the crowd and the gang vanishes into the mists without witnesses identifying them
Scanlan and McMurdo make their way back
McMurdo says it is like a war between them and others

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Sure, it is like a war. What is it but a war between us and them, and we hit back where we best can.

events.label: There is high revel in the lodge room at the Union House over the double killing and the earlier distant triumph; an execution is carried out and completed
The lodge revels in the execution of Ted Baldwin, describing how he was driven home and shot multiple times, then describes a contretemps where a man and wife were spared and made to drive on
Boss McGinty devises a new attack and leads McMurdo aside into an inner room for their first interview
McGinty draws a rough diagram on a page torn from his notebook
McMurdo is commissioned to take over the job involving Chester Wilcox

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Now it’s for you to take it over.

events.label: McGinty tells McMurdo he can take Manders and Reilly

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: You can take two men with you—Manders and Reilly.

events.label: McGinty says Manders and Reilly have been warned for service

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: They have been warned for service.

events.label: McGinty describes Chester Wilcox as the chief foreman of the Iron Dike Company

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: He’s the chief foreman of the Iron Dike Company.

events.label: McGinty says Chester Wilcox is armed and shoots quickly and straight

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: He’s armed and shoots quick and straight, with no questions asked.

events.label: McGinty says Chester Wilcox has a wife, three children, and a hired help at night

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: But at night—well, there he is with his wife, three children, and a hired help.

events.label: McGinty specifies the target house is alone at the Iron Dike crossroad

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: That’s the house—all alone at the Iron Dike crossroad, same as you see here on the map—without another within earshot.

events.label: McGinty says it is no good by day

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: It’s no good by day.

events.label: McGinty says Chester Wilcox shot Jim Carnaway

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Didn’t I tell you he shot Jim Carnaway?

events.label: McGinty says Chester Wilcox shot Jim Carnaway at night

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Carnaway was about his house at night, and he shot him.

events.label: McGinty says Chester Wilcox must be settled and McMurdo agrees to do it

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Of course I will do it.

events.label: McMurdo requests time to see the house and make plans

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, you had best give me a night or two that I may see the house and make my plans.

events.label: McGinty shakes McMurdo’s hand and leaves the job with him

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: I leave it with you.

events.label: McMurdo starts off all alone to prepare for the attempt the same night
McMurdo returns from reconnaissance before daylight
McMurdo interviews Manders and Reilly
Manders, Reilly, and McMurdo meet outside the town with one carrying a sack stuffed with quarry powder
The three men arrive at the lonely house at two in the morning
McMurdo listens at the door of the lonely house
McMurdo leans a powder bag against the door, rips a hole, and attaches a fuse
McMurdo and his two companions run away after lighting the fuse
An explosion occurs at the lonely house and the building collapses
McGinty tells the lodge that Chester Wilcox has been moved and that a guard of police should watch over them
McMurdo says 'Leave him to me' to McGinty

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Leave him to me.

events.label: McMurdo says he will get Chester Wilcox sure if he has to wait a year

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: He’s my man, and I’ll get him sure if I have to wait a year for him.

events.label: A vote of thanks and confidence is passed in full lodge
Newspapers report that Wilcox was shot at from an ambuscade
McMurdo is appointed Inner Deacon
Morris comes to see McMurdo on a Saturday evening in May
Morris asks McMurdo if he can speak freely

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: Can I speak with you freely, Mr. McMurdo?

events.label: McMurdo agrees to let Morris speak freely

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Sure.

events.label: Morris tells McMurdo he has a secret that is burning the life out of him

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I’ve a secret here ... and it is just burning the life out of me ... If I tell it, it will mean murder, for sure. If I don’t, it may bring the end of us all. God help me, but I am near out of my wits over it!

events.label: McMurdo pours whisky into a glass and hands it to Morris
McMurdo tells Morris to let him hear what the secret is

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Now let me hear of it.

events.label: Morris drinks the whisky
Morris tells McMurdo there is a detective on their trail

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: There’s a detective on our trail.

events.label: McMurdo reacts by saying Morris is crazy

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Why, man, you’re crazy

events.label: Morris says the detective is Pinkerton and warns they have no show if Pinkerton men are on their trail

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: No, no, it’s no man of the district ... But you’ve heard of Pinkerton’s? ... you’ve no show when they are on your trail.

events.label: Morris says the Pinkerton business is out for results and will destroy them if a Pinkerton man is deep in it

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: It’s a dead earnest business proposition that’s out for results and keeps out till by hook or crook it gets them. If a Pinkerton man is deep in this business, we are all destroyed.

events.label: Morris says they must kill the detective and that it will be up at the lodge

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: We must kill him.

events.label: McMurdo tells Morris to have the facts and asks who the fellow is, where he is, how Morris heard, and why Morris came to him

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Let’s have the facts. Who is the fellow? Where is he? How did you hear of him? Why did you come to me?

events.label: Morris says he has a letter from an East friend in the telegraph service

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I left good friends behind me, and one of them is in the telegraph service. Here’s a letter that I had from him yesterday.

events.label: Morris says McMurdo can read the top part of the letter

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: It’s this part from the top of the page. You can read it yourself.

events.label: McMurdo reads the letter content about the Scowrers and Pinkerton
Morris tells McMurdo he has told no one else about the letter

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: I have told no one else.

events.label: Morris says his friend may know one or two more people and it is likely lodge members

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: Well, I dare say he knows one or two more. It’s likely enough.

events.label: McMurdo decides he can get on the detective's trail based on a description of Birdy Edwards
McMurdo claims he has got him after hearing the detective details

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: By Gar! ... I’ve got him ... What a fool I was not to know it.

events.label: McMurdo asks Morris to leave the matter in his hands and tells him even Morris's name need not be mentioned

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: See here, Morris, will you leave this thing in my hands? ... Even your name need not be mentioned.

events.label: Morris agrees to let McMurdo take the matter off his hands

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: Sure, if you will only take it off mine.

events.label: McMurdo tells Morris he will run it and take it all on himself as if the letter had come to him

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’ll do that. You can stand right back and let me run it. Even your name need not be mentioned. I’ll take it all on myself, as if it were to me that this letter has come.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Then leave it at that and keep your head shut. Now I’ll get down to the lodge, and we’ll soon make old man Pinkerton sorry for himself.

events.label: Morris leaves after agreeing to keep silent

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: The less you know, Friend Morris, the easier your conscience will be, and the better you will sleep. Ask no questions, and let these things settle themselves. I have hold of it now.

events.label: Every paper which would incriminate McMurdo is destroyed before he leaves the house

Ettie comes out to Morris at the window

communicates.speaker: ettie
communicates.content: Something has happened! Oh, Jack, you are in danger!

events.label: Jack tells Ettie it may be wise to make a move before it gets worse

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Sure, it is not very bad, my sweetheart. And yet it may be wise that we make a move before it is worse.

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: I had news to-night, bad news, and I see trouble coming. ... Things are going to happen in this valley. ... If I go, by day or night, it’s you that must come with me!

events.label: Jack says Ettie must come with him and he will leave her where she can be married later

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: No, no, you shall come with me. If this valley is closed to me and I can never come back, how can I leave you behind, and me perhaps in hiding from the police with never a chance of a message? It’s with me you must come. I know a good woman in the place I come from, and it’s there I’d leave you till we can get married.

events.label: Ettie agrees to come with Jack

communicates.speaker: ettie
communicates.content: Yes, Jack, I will come.

events.label: Jack tells Ettie that when a word reaches her she must drop everything and go to the waiting room at the depot until he comes

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Now, mark you, Ettie, it will be just a word to you, and when it reaches you, you will drop everything and come right down to the waiting room at the depot and stay there till I come for you.

events.label: McMurdo goes on to the lodge
McMurdo passes through the outer guard and inner guard of the lodge
McMurdo enters the lodge and receives a buzz of pleasure and welcome
The lodge leaders are present in the long room
The chairman greets McMurdo and calls for judgment

communicates.speaker: chairman
communicates.content: “Indeed, it’s glad we are to see you, Brother!” and “There’s business here that wants a Solomon in judgment to set it right.”

events.label: A neighbor explains that the business is about Lander and Egan

communicates.speaker: neighbour
communicates.content: “It’s Lander and Egan… They both claim the head money given by the lodge for the shooting of old man Crabbe over at Stylestown, and who’s to say which fired the bullet?”

events.label: McMurdo rises and raises his hand
McGinty states that McMurdo's claim of urgency takes precedence by lodge rules

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: “Brother McMurdo claims urgency,”… “It’s a claim that by the rules of this lodge takes precedence. Now Brother, we attend you.”

events.label: McMurdo takes a letter from his pocket
McMurdo announces urgency to the Bodymaster and Brethren and describes a detective collecting evidence

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Eminent Bodymaster… I claim urgency!” and “Eminent Bodymaster and Brethren… I am the bearer of ill news this day; but it is better that it should be known and discussed… I have information that the most powerful and richest organizations in this state have bound themselves together for our destruction, and that at this very moment there is a Pinkerton detective, one Birdy Edwards, at work in the valley collecting the evidence which may put a rope round the necks of many of us, and send every man in this room into a felon’s cell. That is the situation for the discussion of which I have made a claim of urgency.”

events.label: The chairman asks for McMurdo's evidence

communicates.speaker: chairman
communicates.content: “What is your evidence for this, Brother McMurdo?”

events.label: McMurdo says the evidence is in the letter and reads a passage aloud

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “It is in this letter which has come into my hands,” and he reads aloud: “It is a matter of honour with me that I can give no further particulars about the letter, nor put it into your hands; but I assure you that there is nothing else in it which can affect the interests of the lodge. I put the case before you as it has reached me.”

events.label: A brother says he has heard of Birdy Edwards and that Birdy Edwards is the best man in Pinkerton service

communicates.speaker: older_brethren
communicates.content: “Let me say, Mr. Chairman… that I have heard of Birdy Edwards, and that he has the name of being the best man in the Pinkerton service.”

events.label: McGinty asks whether anyone knows Birdy Edwards by sight

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: “Does anyone know him by sight?”

events.label: McMurdo says he does know Birdy Edwards

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Yes,” said McMurdo, “I do.”

events.label: McMurdo says if they act quickly they can cut the matter short

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “I believe we hold him in the hollow of our hands,” and “If we act quickly and wisely, we can cut this thing short. If I have your confidence and your help, it is little that we have to fear.”

events.label: Baldwin says the detective will not leave the valley

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: “That he never leaves the valley,” said Baldwin.

events.label: McMurdo nods and praises Baldwin

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Good for you, Brother Baldwin.”

events.label: McMurdo proposes discussing the detective issue only in private and requests a trustworthy committee

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Eminent Bodymaster… I would put it to you that this is too vital a thing for us to discuss in open lodge… if so much as a word of gossip got to the ears of this man, there would be an end of any chance of our getting him. I would ask the lodge to choose a trusty committee, Mr. Chairman—yourself… and Brother Baldwin here, and five more. Then I can talk freely of what I know and of what I advise should be done.”

events.label: The proposition is adopted and a committee is chosen
A list of committee members is described
McGinty tells the seven men to begin the discussion privately

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: “Now, McMurdo!”

events.label: McMurdo explains that the detective is known to him under a different name and is lodging at Hobson’s Patch

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “I said just now that I knew Birdy Edwards,”… “I need not tell you that he is not here under that name. He’s a brave man, but not a crazy one. He passes under the name of Steve Wilson, and he is lodging at Hobson’s Patch.”

events.label: McMurdo describes meeting Steve Wilson on the cars and says Wilson claimed to be a reporter

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Because I fell into talk with him… I met him on the cars when I went down the line on Wednesday… He said he was a reporter.”

events.label: McMurdo says he discussed questions and paid information to Steve Wilson and describes a promise of more payment

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Wanted to know all he could about the Scowrers and what he called ‘the outrages’ for a New York paper… ‘I’d pay for it and pay well,’ said he… I said what I thought would please him best, and he handed me a twenty-dollar bill for my information. ‘There’s ten times that for you,’ said he, ‘if you can find me all that I want.’”

events.label: McMurdo says he followed Steve Wilson to Hobson’s Patch and saw him leaving the telegraph bureau

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “He got out at Hobson’s Patch, and so did I… I chanced into the telegraph bureau, and he was leaving it.”

events.label: A plan is proposed to locate Steve Wilson by using the telegraph operator and offering lodge secrets for a price

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Why not go right down now and fix him?”… “I’ll go to the Patch to-morrow morning. I’ll find him through the operator… Well, then I’ll tell him that I’m a Freeman myself. I’ll offer him all the secrets of the lodge for a price… He’ll see that that’s horse sense. Let him come at ten o’clock at night, and he shall see everything. That will fetch him sure.”

events.label: McMurdo instructs the seven men to come by nine o’clock to trap Steve Wilson

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “You can plan the rest for yourselves… If I get his promise—and I’ll let you know if I do—I’d have the whole seven of you come to me by nine o’clock… We’ll get him in.”

events.label: The group decides to be with McMurdo at nine tomorrow and to handle the rest after the door closes behind Steve Wilson

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: “Leave it at that, McMurdo. At nine to-morrow we’ll be with you. You once get the door shut behind him, and you can leave the rest with us.”

events.label: Narration states McMurdo's residence is a lonely house suited for the planned crime
McMurdo goes to Hobson’s Patch as agreed
McMurdo refuses to speak with Captain Marvin when Captain Marvin addresses him at the station

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: Captain Marvin addresses him while he waits at the station; McMurdo turns away and refuses to speak.

events.label: McMurdo returns in the afternoon and tells McGinty that Steve Wilson is coming

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “He is coming,” he said.

events.label: McGinty responds that it is good

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: “Good!”

events.label: McMurdo explains that Steve Wilson has been in the area for at least six weeks and may have passed on results

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Do you reckon he knows much?”… “McMurdo shook his head gloomily.” and “He’s been here some time—six weeks at the least… If he has been working among us all that time… I should expect that he has got results, and that he has passed them on.”

events.label: McGinty proposes sending boys to give Morris a beating up to see what Morris can be made to say

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: “I’ve a mind to send a couple of the boys round before evening to give him a beating up and see what they can get from him.”

events.label: McMurdo agrees there would be no harm in beating up Morris but says it is not for him to stand between Morris and the others

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Well, there would be no harm in that,”… “I won’t deny that I have a liking for Morris and would be sorry to see him come to harm… But still it is not for me to stand between him and you.”

events.label: McGinty says he will fix Morris

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: “I’ll fix the old devil!”… “I’ve had my eye on him this year past.”

events.label: McMurdo says they must lie low until the Pinkerton affair is settled and cannot afford police attention today

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “But whatever you do must be to-morrow; for we must lie low until the Pinkerton affair is settled up. We can’t afford to set the police buzzing, to-day of all days.”

events.label: McMurdo produces a wad of dollar notes
McMurdo claims he did not bring papers and says he filled Steve Wilson up about rules and forms of membership

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “What papers?”… “Well, there are no papers. But I filled him up about constitutions and books of rules and forms of membership. He expects to get right down to the end of everything before he leaves.”

events.label: McMurdo states Steve Wilson will be met by McMurdo at ten o'clock, tapped three times, and brought behind the door

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “He comes at ten. He is to tap three times, and me to open the door for him. Then I’ll get behind him and shut it. He’s our man then.”

events.label: McMurdo outlines a trapping plan involving seven men, faked papers, and a fight over the pistol arm

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “And the next step wants considering… Suppose I show him right into a room with seven men in it… There is going to be shooting… This is how I should work it. You will all be in the big room… I’ll open the door for him, show him into the parlour beside the door, and leave him there while I get the papers… Then I will go back to him with some faked papers. As he is reading them I will jump for him and get my grip on his pistol arm. You’ll hear me call and in you will rush… But I allow that I can hold him till you come.”

events.label: McMurdo cleans, oils, and loads his Smith & Wesson revolver
McMurdo surveys the apartment where the detective will be trapped
McMurdo discusses the intended trap with Scanlan and warns him to take a night off and keep clear

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: “Scanlan… McMurdo told him shortly what was intended.” and “And if I were you, Mike Scanlan, I would take a night off and keep clear of it. There will be bloody work here before morning.”

events.label: Scanlan answers Mac

communicates.speaker: scanlan
communicates.content: Well, indeed then, Mac,

events.label: Scanlan states he lacks nerve

communicates.speaker: scanlan
communicates.content: It’s not the will but the nerve that is wanting in me.

events.label: Scanlan states he saw Manager Dunn go down at the colliery

communicates.speaker: scanlan
communicates.content: When I saw Manager Dunn go down at the colliery yonder it was just more than I could stand.

events.label: Scanlan states he is not made for it

communicates.speaker: scanlan
communicates.content: I’m not made for it, same as you or McGinty.

events.label: Scanlan agrees to leave if the lodge will not think worse of him

communicates.speaker: scanlan
communicates.content: If the lodge will think none the worse of me, I’ll just do as you advise and leave you to yourselves for the evening.

events.label: Men come in good time as arranged
McMurdo has men assembled under his roof for the killing of the Pinkerton detective
McMurdo places whisky upon the table
Baldwin and Cormac are half-drunk as liquor primes them for work
Cormac places his hands on the stove for an instant
Cormac says that will do

communicates.speaker: tiger_cormac
communicates.content: That will do

events.label: Baldwin says he will have the truth out of him if he is strapped

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: If he is strapped to that, we will have the truth out of him.

events.label: McMurdo says they will have the truth out of him

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: We’ll have the truth out of him, never fear,

events.label: Boss approves and says McMurdo is to handle the man

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: You are the one to handle him,

events.label: Boss says the man will not get a warning until his hand is on the throat and mentions shutters

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Not a warning will he get till your hand is on his throat. It’s a pity there are no shutters to your windows.

events.label: McMurdo draws the curtains tighter
Secretary says it is close upon the hour and maybe he will not come

communicates.speaker: harraway
communicates.content: Maybe he won’t come. Maybe he’ll get a sniff of danger

events.label: McMurdo answers that he will come

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: He’ll come, never fear,

events.label: McMurdo says he is as eager to come as they are to see him and calls attention to sounds

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: He is as eager to come as you can be to see him. Hark to that!

events.label: Hands are laid upon weapons and McMurdo warns not to make a sound

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Not a sound, for your lives!

events.label: McMurdo goes from the room, closing the door carefully behind him
Murderers wait with strained ears while McMurdo counts steps down the passage
McMurdo opens the outer door and greets an arrival
A strange step occurs inside and an unfamiliar voice is heard
The door slams and the key turns in the lock
Tiger Cormac laughs and Boss McGinty tells him to be quiet

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Be quiet, you fool! You’ll be the undoing of us yet!

events.label: McMurdo returns and appears with his finger upon his lip
Boss McGinty asks whether Birdy Edwards is there

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Is he here? Is Birdy Edwards here?

events.label: McMurdo answers that he is Birdy Edwards

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Yes, Birdy Edwards is here. I am Birdy Edwards!

events.label: Rifle barrels break through each window and curtains are torn from their hangings
Boss McGinty roars and plunges for the half-opened door
Captain Marvin of the Mine Police levels a revolver at the Boss
Boss recoils and falls back into his chair
McMurdo tells the Boss he is safer in his position and warns Baldwin to take his hand off his pistol

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: You’re safer there, Councillor. And you, Baldwin, if you don’t take your hand off your pistol, you’ll cheat the hangman yet. Pull it out, or by the Lord that made me—There, that will do.

events.label: McMurdo says there are forty armed men around the house and orders Marvin to take their pistols

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: There are forty armed men round this house, and you can figure it out for yourself what chance you have. Take their pistols, Marvin!

events.label: Men are disarmed under the menace of rifles
The trapped men sit disarmed around the table
Birdy Edwards tells them they may not meet again until the courthouse stand

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’d like to say a word to you before we separate. I guess we may not meet again until you see me on the stand in the courthouse.

events.label: Birdy Edwards identifies himself as Birdy Edwards of Pinkerton’s and says he was chosen to break up the gang

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’ll give you something to think over between now and then. I am Birdy Edwards! I was chosen to break up your gang.

events.label: Birdy Edwards states his game was played secretly and that only Captain Marvin and his employers knew

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I had a hard and dangerous game to play. Not a soul, not one soul, not my nearest and dearest, knew that I was playing it. Only Captain Marvin here and my employers knew that.

events.label: Birdy Edwards claims the job is over tonight and that he is the winner

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: But it’s over to-night, thank God, and I am the winner!

events.label: Birdy Edwards tells them some will take no further hand and that sixty more besides will see a jail this night

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, I take my chance of that. Anyhow, some of you will take no further hand, and there are sixty more besides yourselves that will see a jail this night.

events.label: Birdy Edwards states he went to Chicago and was made one

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: They told me it was to do with the Freemen; so I went to Chicago and was made one.

events.label: Birdy Edwards states he joined the lodge and took his share in councils

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: So I joined your infernal lodge, and I took my share in your councils.

events.label: Birdy Edwards tells them that his employers and Captain Marvin knew and that it is over

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I could not save Dunn and Menzies, for I did not know enough; but I will see that their murderers are hanged.

events.label: Birdy Edwards orders Marvin to take the men in and get it over

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Now, Marvin, I’ll keep you no more. Take them in and get it over.

events.label: Scanlan is given a sealed note to be left at Miss Ettie Shafter’s address
A woman and a muffled man board a special train sent by the railroad company and travel out of the land of danger
Ettie and her lover set foot in the Valley of Fear for the last time
Ettie and her lover are married in Chicago with old Jacob Shafter as witness
The trial of the Scowrers is held far from where their adherents might terrify the guardians of the law
In vain, lodge money is spent like water to attempt to save the Scowrers
McGinty meets his fate on the scaffold
Eight of McGinty’s chief followers share his fate
Fifty-odd are imprisoned for various degrees
Work of Birdy Edwards is completed
Ted Baldwin escapes the scaffold and so do the Willabys and other fiercest spirits
Edwards is chased from Chicago and goes under a changed name to California; he works with an English partner Barker and amasses a fortune
A warning arrives that bloodhounds are on his track and he clears for England
In the epilogue, the police trial passes and John Douglas is referred to a higher court
Holmes writes to Mrs. Douglas to get her husband out of England at any cost

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: Get him out of England at any cost,

events.label: Holmes writes that there is no safety for her husband in England

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: There is no safety for your husband in England.

events.label: An enigmatic note is slipped into the letter box
The note says “Dear me, Mr. Holmes. Dear me!”

communicates.speaker: enigmatic_note
communicates.content: Dear me, Mr. Holmes. Dear me!

events.label: Mrs. Hudson brings a message that a gentleman wishes to see Mr. Holmes

communicates.speaker: mrs_hudson
communicates.content: a gentleman wished to see Mr. Holmes, and that the matter was of the utmost importance.

events.label: Cecil Barker reports he has bad news and says it is terrible

communicates.speaker: cecil_barker
communicates.content: I’ve had bad news—terrible news, Mr. Holmes,

events.label: Barker says he has had a note from someone who has

communicates.speaker: cecil_barker
communicates.content: I have had a note from someone who has.

events.label: Barker tells Holmes that Douglas was lost overboard off St. Helena

communicates.speaker: cecil_barker
communicates.content: It’s poor Douglas. They tell me his name is Edwards; but he will always be Jack Douglas of Benito Canyon to me. I told you that they started together for South Africa in the Palmyra three weeks ago. The ship reached Cape Town last night. I received this cable from Mrs. Douglas this morning: “Jack has been lost overboard in gale off St. Helena. No one knows how accident occurred. “IVY DOUGLAS.”

events.label: Holmes remarks that the note came in that way and comments it was likely well stage-managed

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: Ha! It came like that, did it? Well, I’ve no doubt it was well stage-managed.

events.label: Holmes tells Barker the crime is from London, not from America

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: This crime is from London, not from America.

events.label: Holmes says the Americans took Moriarty’s consultant into partnership and their man was doomed

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: These Americans were well advised... they took into partnership, as any foreign criminal could do, this great consultant in crime. From that moment their man was doomed.

events.label: Holmes tells Barker he was right and that he needs time

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: You heard me warn this man at Birlstone Manor House that the coming danger was greater than the past. Was I right? ... But you must give me time—you must give me time!

clues.significance: Holmes deciphered the cipher using Whitaker’s Almanac page 534, column two to produce a message referencing 'Douglas' and 'Birlstone'.
Holmes explained to the inspector the facts about the letter and the cipher during discussion of the Birlstone mystery, linking the cipher to the investigation
The card with initials V.V. and number 341 is found beside the dead man, being treated as left behind by the murderer
Holmes relied on the presence of the card labeled V.V. 341 as part of his reconstruction of the events at the Manor House
Holmes examined the blood mark on the sill with a lens.
Holmes inferred the shoe tread and a broad splay-foot impression from the footmark pattern visible in the mud-stained corner.
Holmes placed a slipper upon the blood mark on the sill and found it corresponded exactly
Holmes stated that the blood mark on the windowsill was deliberately placed by Barker to give a false clue to the police.
Holmes located a sodden bundle weighted with a dumb-bell under the writing table and identified it as the object Barker had raised from the bottom of the moat.
Holmes used the clothing items and the overcoat/tailor’s tab information during his exposition while presenting evidence related to the investigation.
